claim.summary: TESSA extracts numerical and textual features, selects salient features, and generates general then domain-specific temporal annotations.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; 3.1 Multi-modal Feature Extraction
source_evidence.quote: We extract fea- tures from time series data through a structured process Mr. Formally, for each channel c ∈C, the set of time-series features Ft is denoted as: Ft = {f 1 t , · · · , f nt t } = Mr(X), (1) where Mr denotes the feature extraction frame- work applied to X, fi t is the i-th extracted feature of X, and nt is the number of extracted features.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.6; 3.3 Domain-specific annotation
source_evidence.quote: To improve the quality of domain-specific annotations and ensure better alignment with general annotations, we introduce an annotation reviewer. This LLM, Mrev, reviews the generated annotations and extracted terms, pro- viding feedback ef to the extractor and annotator: ef = Mrev(prev(eg, et, {J i} nJ i=1)), (10) where prev is the prompt for reviewing annotations.

citation.authors: Jiang, Yushan and Yu, Wenchao and Lee, Geon and Song, Dongjin and Shin, Kijung and Cheng, Wei and Liu, Yanchi and Chen, Haifeng

claim.summary: TimeXL fuses prototype-based multimodal predictions with an LLM and iteratively refines textual context using training/validation feedback.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.6; 3.3.1 Fused Predictions
source_evidence.quote: We compile the final prediction based on a fusion of both the multi-modal encoder Menc and prediction LLM Mpred. source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; Section 3.2, Overview
source_evidence.quote: Aion ∞is built from six component groups: agents, skills, rules, memory, evaluation, and protocols. Agents are the front-end roles that drive interpretation, evidence collection, solution construction, and review. Skills provide reusable priors and structured workflows that stabilize execution across the lifecycle. Rules define the admissible boundary of the workflow. Memory records progress, decisions, and structural state so that long executions do not drift. Evaluation turns runs into explicit assessment through suites, graders, and final acceptance checks.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; Section 3.2 continued
source_evidence.quote: specify how work, review, rechecking, stop signals, and memory updates communicate between different sessions. Together, these six groups constitute the harness that answers Q2. In our implementation, each group contains several named components, which are expanded in Appendix B.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; Section 3.1, Validation interface, Eq. (3)
source_evidence.quote: Validation interface. V maps a candidate output o to (g, s) = V(o), (3) where g records validity checks such as timestamp alignment, leakage boundaries, or format compliance, and s records scored metrics such as forecasting error, profit, or report quality. A candidate is admissible only when all validity checks in g pass, and admissible candidates are ranked by s.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; Section 3.3.1, Temporal Grounding
source_evidence.quote: Temporal grounding concerns the parts that are closest to the time series itself. Before asking which model to use, the harness must first determine what counts as one temporal observation, which horizon is requested, and whether the visible data can support that request. In this paper, temporal constraints are the time-related requirements that any valid answer must satisfy, including the observation unit, allowed history and cutoff, forecast or reasoning horizon, timestamp granularity, output frequency, and leakage boundary.

source_evidence.quote: Unlike conventional tool- augmented agents that must pass data through lan- guage messages, TIMECLAW executes these oper- ations inside the harness runtime, where the full time-series object already resides in the workspace W. In prac- tice, forecasters combine quantitative event attributes, such as rainfall amount, with in- sights from similar historical cases to estimate plausible ranges of peak flow and flood volume. To make this process explicit, the skill is organized into four computational

citation.title: CastFSR: A Fast--Slow--Reflect Agentic Reasoning Framework for Context-Aware Time Series Forecasting
citation.authors: Xiaoyu Tao and Mingyue Cheng and Bokai Pan and Chuang Jiang and Huanjian Zhang and Tian Gao and Yaguo Liu and Qi Liu and Enhong Chen

claim.summary: Fast-slow-reflect orchestration of numerical forecast priors and contextual revision.
claim.evidence_basis: Primary-source method passages; locators in source_evidence_json and reviewed_modules_json

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; Introduction, framework overview
source_evidence.quote: In fast-thinking forecasting, CastFSR pro- files historical observations and autonomously selects suit- able lightweight forecasters to construct a data-driven fore- cast prior. In slow deliberative reasoning, it retrieves future- relevant evidence from long-range contextual histories, adap- tively identifies context-specific look-back windows, and rea- sons about how contextual factors reshape future dynamics to refine the forecast prior. In reflective evaluation, CastFSR it- eratively evaluates and adjusts candidate forecasts to enforce temporal regularities, contextual consistency, and domain constraints.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; Model-Agnostic Instantiation of CastFSR, training paragraph
source_evidence.quote: Specifically, we internalize the workflow in a small model through two-stage training. First, SFT learns executable Fast–Slow–Reflect be- havior from general LLM trajectories distilled on the full cross-domain training data. The validation removes trajecto- ries with illegal tool calls, incorrect stage order, ground-truth leakage, invalid timestamps, or incomplete forecasts. Second, multi-turn RL optimizes complete decision trajectories un- der delayed forecasting feedback.

harness.primary_contribution: Forecaster selection and context-conditioned forecast refinement

citation.title: SCENARIODIFF: A Scenario-level Guidance Framework for Multimodal Time Series Forecasting--Extended Version
citation.authors: Tuan-Binh Tran and Dat Nguyen Cong and Duc-Trong Le and Thanh Trung Huynh and Tung Kieu

claim.summary: Historical summaries, future scenarios and sparse anchors guide probabilistic diffusion forecasts.
claim.evidence_basis: Primary-source method passages; locators in source_evidence_json and reviewed_modules_json

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; Section IV.A, Framework Overview
source_evidence.quote: SCENARIODIFF organizes contextual reasoning into three hi- erarchical levels. First, a frozen Historical Context Agent maps M1:L to stepwise context summaries sctx 1:L, grounding the model in document-aligned historical evidence. Second, a frozen Scenario Agent maps (x1:L, sctx 1:L) to a scenario description sscn, projecting a coarse qualitative prior over the forecast horizon. Third, an Anchor Guidance Agent maps (x1:L, sctx 1:L, sscn) to sparse anchor points A, which provide localized constraints for inference-time trajectory refinement.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; Section IV.A, Framework Overview
source_evidence.quote: During denoising, the model receives the observed history x1:L, the noisy future x(t), and the contextual conditions produced by the Historical Context Agent and the Scenario Agent. Starting from Gaussian noise, the reverse process generates a trajectory consistent with both numerical history and scenario-level context. Anchor points A are then used by Anchor Blended Sampling to locally refine the generated trajectory.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; Section IV.A, Framework Overview
source_evidence.quote: SCENARIODIFF organizes contextual reasoning into three hi- erarchical levels. First, a frozen Historical Context Agent maps M1:L to stepwise context summaries sctx 1:L, grounding the model in document-aligned historical evidence. Second, a frozen Scenario Agent maps (x1:L, sctx 1:L) to a scenario description sscn, projecting a coarse qualitative prior over the forecast horizon. Third, an Anchor Guidance Agent maps (x1:L, sctx 1:L, sscn) to sparse anchor points A, which provide localized constraints for inference-time trajectory refinement.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; Section IV.A, Framework Overview
source_evidence.quote: During denoising, the model receives the observed history x1:L, the noisy future x(t), and the contextual conditions produced by the Historical Context Agent and the Scenario Agent. Starting from Gaussian noise, the reverse process generates a trajectory consistent with both numerical history and scenario-level context. Anchor points A are then used by Anchor Blended Sampling to locally refine the generated trajectory.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; Section 3.5, FTAgent execution paragraph
source_evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 2, FTAGENT composes pro- grams to train each forecaster with a grid search of hyperparameters. It organizes training jobs – i.e., (forecaster, hyperparameter, dataset) triplets – into a queue and assigns available GPUs for maximally parallel execution. During training, it monitors pro- cesses, resolves errors when encountered, and re- covers interrupted jobs without human intervention. This procedure ends when the queue is emptied.

citation.title: Moirai Agent
citation.authors: {Salesforce AI Research}

claim.summary: The official project documents two composable agents: contextual forecast adaptation and forecasting-expert selection.

source_evidence.locator: README paragraphs 1–2; fetched 2026-10-15
source_evidence.quote: Moirai agent supports two core capabilities. First, it enables context-aware forecasting by combining numerical history with external contextual inputs to refine lookback windows, detect anomalies, and anticipate future effects. Second, it performs expert selection through an LLM-based selector that chooses the most suitable forecasting model for each task from a pool of state-of-the-art forecasters.

citation.title: MERIT: Multi-Agent Collaboration for Unsupervised Time Series Representation Learning
citation.authors: Zhou, Shu and Xuan, Yunyang and Ao, Yuxuan and Wang, Xin and Fan, Tao and Wang, Hao

claim.summary: Agents retrieve related series, select augmentations and review positive views for contrastive representation learning.
claim.evidence_basis: Primary-source method passages; locators in source_evidence_json and reviewed_modules_json

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; Figure 2 caption
source_evidence.quote: Our retrieval agent first selects neighborhood candidates with similarity, followed by refinement using an LLM. Our augmentation agent then selects suitable data augmentation strategies from the augmentation strategy library. Finally, our review agent evaluates the quality of the augmented sequences, which approves positive samples into a memory bank and returns to the retrieval agent for refinement if rejected. The augmented views and neighboring samples are utilized as positives for time series representation learning.

claim.summary: PandaAI combines a regime-conditioned finance LLM with constrained alpha-factor search, portfolio execution and feedback-based rule/model adaptation.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.17; passage beginning "Regime-Conditioned Instruction Tuning"
source_evidence.quote: Regime-Conditioned Instruction Tuning A financial instruction dataset DSFT is constructed where each sample v is tagged with the originating market state zt from Module M. Each sample v contains three components (x, y, zt), where x denotes the question and y corresponds to the answer. This teaches the model to condition financial concepts on market context. The same underlying concept must be implemented differ- ently

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "We conceptualize Alpha Mining"
source_evidence.quote: We conceptualize Alpha Mining not as creative writing, but as a Constrained Search Problem over a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of operators. We implement an LLM- guided Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) framework to navigate this sparse solution space. The process ensures robustness through four quant-specific phases that incorporate the constraint set C and the market state zt at distinct checkpoints (visualized in Figure 2);

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "Portfolio Optimization (P)"
source_evidence.quote: Portfolio Optimization (P) We solve the regime-conditioned convex problem: wt = arg max w∈Cport(wTst −λ(zt) · wTΣw) (1) where λ(zt) automatically increases during high-volatility regimes to prioritize capital preservation. Execution Control (E) To minimize implementation shortfall (IS), the execution pol- icy πexec(a|wt, zt) selects strategies (e.g., TWAP, VWAP) isomorphic to the inferred liquid- ity profile. This closes the ”simulation-to-reality” gap by accounting for market friction.

citation.title: Have an LLM Write Your Anomaly Detector: Autonomous Discovery of Compact, Interpretable Detectors for Time Series
citation.authors: Berghaus, David

claim.summary: An LLM-driven autonomous research loop repeatedly edits one NumPy anomaly-detector program, scores each edit on synthetic anomalies injected into a held-out slice of the training region, and returns the best-scoring compact detector.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "an LLM-driven agent that edits"
source_evidence.quote: an LLM-driven agent that edits and re-evaluates a single program with no human intervention. A fixed harness defines the data interface, the validation objective, and the scoring code. The language model is allowed to edit only the detector program. In each iteration it (i) inspects the current detector program and its recent scores, (ii) proposes a concrete modification,

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "Detector representation. Each candidate detector"
source_evidence.quote: Detector representation. Each candidate detector is a selfcontained Python and NumPy function with a fixed signature: it consumes a training segment and a test segment of a series and returns a per-timestep anomaly score.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "The search uses no real"
source_evidence.quote: The search uses no real anomaly labels. Candidates are scored by detecting synthetic anomalies injected only into a held-out slice of each series’ training region. The generator is an explicit prior over what an anomaly can look like. We aim for anomalies that are realistic in the mechanism that produces them, like a sensor that freezes, a valid shape appearing out of context, a cycle at the wrong period or phase.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "Synthetic anomalies are injected and"
source_evidence.quote: Synthetic anomalies are injected and labeled only in a held-out slice of the training region, and these labels are used only for validation; no real labels or official-test-suffix data enter the search.

review_audit.title_checked: EpiWorld: Grounding LLM Policy Agents in Epidemiological World Models
review_audit.claim_summary: EpiWorld grounds an LLM policy actor in a graph-structured, action-conditioned epidemiological world model and a tiered skill library of protocol constraints, surveillance estimators and after-action lessons, using counterfactual rollouts to evaluate and refine weekly regional intervention policies.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: Weekly state-level surveillance for 51 US states (COVID-19, Dec 2020-Feb 2022) plus calibrated COVID-19 and influenza SEIR simulators; the world model is scored by MAE and Peak-MAE on 12-week autoregressive rollouts (in-distribution and temporal/state/intervention OOD) against compartmental, latent-ODE and neural-CDE forecasters, and policies by 8-week cumulative hospitalisation reduction relative to the historical policy against three RL/genetic-programming planners, with six LLM backbones and re-execution in the generating SEIR simulator.
corrections: Policy gains are measured in simulation: inside the learned world model and, for the synthetic COVID-19 SEIR state-OOD split, re-executed in the generating simulator; the Real-US data admit no ground-truth generator, so the reported up-to-59% hospitalisation reduction does not establish real-world outcomes.
Adaptive Lessons are regime-specific: a bank mined under Omicron degraded first-wave outcomes by 12.1%, so the authors mine a separate lesson bank per infection setting.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "As optimization proceeds, evaluated strategies"
source_evidence.quote: As optimization proceeds, evaluated strategies and their backtest outcomes accumulate in the archive Ak . source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "When ηk = ηlarge"
source_evidence.quote: When ηk = ηlarge , the LLM is instructed to make substantial changes to the core trading logic, and the resulting strategy is implemented as a full rewrite of the base program. source_evidence.quote: Cross-Period Robust Objective (CPRO) promotes temporal robustness by evaluating strategies across calendar-year windows. source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "By emphasizing lower-tail performance"
source_evidence.quote: By emphasizing lower-tail performance, CPRO prevents strong results in favorable periods from fully compensating for poor performance elsewhere, thereby promoting robustness across market periods.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Memory-Guided Expansion and Filtering: The"

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "Notably, all retrieved exogenous events"

(2026), whose reliability is verified through human expert audit. This chronological constraint explicitly prevents look-ahead bias.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Here, Φmem updates M𝑡 to"
source_evidence.quote: Here, Φmem updates M𝑡 to refine future search queries (M𝑡ret ) and noise filters (M𝑡sel ), while Φknow derives general causal forecasting rules from past errors to update the persistent knowledge base K𝑡 . The detailed reflection prompt template are provided in Figure 7 and 8 in Appendix B. Both operators initially append new insights.

review_audit.title_checked: SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting
review_audit.claim_summary: SEER conditions a frozen LLM forecaster on retrieved events and turns forecast residuals into two decoupled textual updates, a retrieval/selection memory and a persistent causal knowledge base, both indexed up to the forecast cut-off.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: Six domains (weather and electricity 7-day, stock next-day direction, memory/SSD prices 6/9 months, Polymarket probabilities) with chronological learning/evaluation windows; MAE/MSE, accuracy and Brier score against seven deep forecasters, six LLM-based forecasters, TimesFM 3.0 and Chronos-2, plus no-event and event-RAG ablations over four backbone LLMs.
corrections: The look-ahead guard on retrieved events reuses LEAF's fact-checking filter; SEER's own contribution is the error-driven memory and knowledge updates, which are frozen during backtesting.
Polymarket event probabilities and selective three-class stock direction are part of the six domains; numerical time-series gains rest on the weather, electricity and component-price series.
review_audit.notes: Identity and selected method/evaluation passages checked against local PDF text; not an independent reproduction of reported results.

citation.title: EvoCast: Reliable Autonomous Research Agents for Iterative Forecasting Architecture Evolution
citation.authors: Xu, Kaipeng and Yan, Xianli and Wang, Yan and Liu, Xiang and Liu, Shan

claim.summary: EvoCast runs a fixed-protocol research loop in which LLM agents propose and implement forecasting-architecture changes while deterministic program authorities validate source boundaries, run canonical evaluation, gate promotion and write outcome-typed evidence.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.13; passage beginning "This separation defines three permissions."
source_evidence.quote: This separation defines three permissions. LLM agents can generate research intent and code changes. Builder edits must remain inside the fixed editable boundary. Experimental facts, metrics, promotion decisions, and model-state updates are confirmed only by program authorities. Agent self-report does not directly become an experimental conclusion.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.13; passage beginning "The dataset loader, split definition,"
source_evidence.quote: The dataset loader, split definition, metric computation, training schedule, evaluation runner, and promotion logic remain frozen outside the Builder’s editable scope. Each candidate first passes source-boundary validation before canonical evaluation is launched.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "The update 𝑈 (·) writes"
source_evidence.quote: The update 𝑈 (·) writes model state, mechanism evidence, and engineering memory according to the outcome. An accepted candidate becomes the incumbent, with its supporting formal metrics and gate decision recorded. A rejected candidate leaves the incumbent unchanged and records an executed hypothesis that did not improve the metric as a valid negative.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Model state changes only after"
source_evidence.quote: Model state changes only after promotion, while evidence state accumulates valid improvements, negatives, unstable gains, and failure records, allowing subsequent planning to use the full research trajectory.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.14; passage beginning "Task and Protocol Initialization. Each"
source_evidence.quote: Task and Protocol Initialization. Each autonomous run starts from a fixed task protocol. Before research begins, the system fixes the dataset, target, lookback, horizon, forecasting mode, metric, training budget, research-round budget, and repair budget.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.14; passage beginning "Executed Mechanism Ablation. Baseline diagnosis"
source_evidence.quote: Executed Mechanism Ablation. Baseline diagnosis converts the active baseline from a comparison anchor into mechanism evidence. EvoCast first analyzes the active prediction path and then uses the Baseline-Diagnosis Planner to generate runnable mechanismablation targets. Each ablation target is tied to a concrete source region, an ablation action, and an input-output preservation contract.

harness.primary_contribution: EvoCast runs a fixed-protocol research loop in which LLM agents propose and implement forecasting-architecture changes while deterministic program authorities validate source boundaries, run canonical evaluation, gate promotion and write outcome-typed evidence.

contributions.GH: Cognition-authority separated promotion chain; Outcome-typed research evidence and failure memory
contributions.TSK: Forecast-protocol grounding and baseline mechanism ablation

review_audit.claim_summary: EvoCast runs a fixed-protocol research loop in which LLM agents propose and implement forecasting-architecture changes while deterministic program authorities validate source boundaries, run canonical evaluation, gate promotion and write outcome-typed evidence.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: RQ1: 30 idea-to-code tasks over 10 forecasting backbones against direct editing, mini-SWE-agent, AIDE, R&D-Agent and AutoResearch (success, fidelity, repair, tokens, cost, time); RQ2: Air Quality, Melbourne Pedestrian T33 and Steel Industry under TFB with 7:1:2 splits, normalized MSE/MAE against Sundial, Toto-2.0, Time-VLM, TimeCMA, AIDE and R&D-Agent within a 20-round cap; RQ3: five system ablations on Melbourne T33; MiniMax-M3 backend.
corrections: RQ2 gains are 2.0-12.1% MSE reductions over each run's own selected baseline on three single-dataset cases (seed 2027); they do not establish general architecture superiority across benchmarks.
The text gives a 7:1:2 split but does not state which split the promotion gate reads, so reported test scores should not be assumed to be untouched by selection.

citation.title: Zero-Shot Time-Series Question Answering via Decoupled Perception and Reasoning
citation.authors: Xie, Jing and Yuan, Haochen and Wang, Yunbo

claim.summary: TSHarness decouples numerical perception from question answering: a Perceiver populates a tool-grounded Time-Series Perception State, an Answerer reasons over it and requests targeted re-perception, and a PPO-trained selector prunes tool calls, all built on one source benchmark and frozen for zero-shot transfer.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "The TPS defines a standardized"
source_evidence.quote: The TPS defines a standardized interface for reading measured series properties and adding questionspecific analyses. A stable core organizes statistical and temporal fields, while named extensions retain the scope and results of additional calculations.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Evidence grounding. Within the core"
source_evidence.quote: Evidence grounding. Within the core C, ιj stores metadata (series identities, channel configurations, and valid temporal spans); Sj and Fj record statistical summaries (e.g., mean, variance, quantile bounds) and temporal primitives (e.g., trend monotonicity, dominant frequencies, prominent changepoints), respectively; and hj is an LLM-generated summary.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "The A NSWERER then reasons"
source_evidence.quote: The A NSWERER then reasons over the accumulated TPS and question context to synthesize the final output. Crucially, when existing evidence is deemed insufficient, the A NSWERER initiates an iterative feedback loop back to the P ERCEIVER, requesting targeted, fine-grained measurements.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Unsupported, duplicate, or out-of-budget requests"
source_evidence.quote: Unsupported, duplicate, or out-of-budget requests are rejected. 3. Constrained answer synthesis. The A NSWERER can commit a response at any iteration and proceeds with the available state when the request budget is exhausted.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "Furthermore, to mitigate redundant computational"
source_evidence.quote: Furthermore, to mitigate redundant computational overhead, a lightweight reinforcement-learning (RL) T OOL S ELECTOR adaptively prunes sub-optimal tool proposals by balancing answer correctness against execution latency on source tasks.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "Once trained on source tasks,"
source_evidence.quote: Once trained on source tasks, the parameters θ of the T OOL S ELECTOR are frozen alongside the backbone LLM, delivering an adaptive, cost-effective perception frontend across all zero-shot target evaluations.

harness.primary_contribution: TSHarness decouples numerical perception from question answering: a Perceiver populates a tool-grounded Time-Series Perception State, an Answerer reasons over it and requests targeted re-perception, and a PPO-trained selector prunes tool calls, all built on one source benchmark and frozen for zero-shot transfer.

contributions.GH: Evidence-gap re-perception loop; Cost-aware RL tool selector

review_audit.title_checked: Zero-Shot Time-Series Question Answering via Decoupled Perception and Reasoning

review_audit.evaluation_summary: Built on TSRBench and transferred zero-shot to Time-MQA, ChatTime, CaTSBench, TSAQA and TimeOmni (412-question subsets for agentic comparisons); accuracy with Qwen3.8-27B and GPT-5.6-sol against zero-shot, CoT, ReAct, TimeClaw and in-domain ChatTime/Time-MQA checkpoints, plus tool/memory ablations, re-perception and tool-cost analyses.
corrections: Tools, memory and the selector are developed with TSRBench ground-truth answers, so only the five target benchmarks are zero-shot; with GPT-5.6-sol accuracy falls on TimeOmni and memory gives no average gain on targets.
Agentic baselines are compared on fixed 412-question subsets per target, so these numbers are not full-benchmark scores.

review_audit.claim_summary: SOTA post-trains Qwen3.8-27B with teacher-trajectory SFT and GRPO to choose among nine option-strategy families from a point-in-time option-implied market state, while deterministic resolvers turn each choice into contracts, position sizes and delta hedges.

citation.title: SciExam for ENSO: Can AI Agents Build Climate Models?
citation.authors: Zhang, Yinling and Liu, Langchen and Xiu, Dongbin and Zou, Xueyan and Kuang, Xu and Wang, Mengdi and Liu, Shilong

claim.summary: SciExam for ENSO has agents turn raw ocean-atmosphere observations into five monthly ENSO indices, write and freeze their own diagnostics, and build a low-order stochastic model that hidden graders score against a published reference on statistics, withheld-variable reconstruction and held-out forecasts.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "Third, agents generate their own"
source_evidence.quote: Third, agents generate their own feedback by developing diagnostics from the task’s scientific guidance. The diagnostics are frozen before model development: agents may execute them to assess each revision but cannot modify them, which prevents their evaluation criteria from drifting toward their results. Grader scores and held-out data remain inaccessible throughout the run.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "SciExam for ENSO mirrors a"
source_evidence.quote: SciExam for ENSO mirrors a research setting in which a scientist receives observations, background material, and a modeling objective, and must decide how to build and assess a model. Its design separates the task-specific materials, namely the data, instructions, and graders, from a general execution protocol, so the same structure can be applied to other modeling problems.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "First, hidden graders evaluate each"
source_evidence.quote: First, hidden graders evaluate each model on three complementary aspects: whether its free-running simulations reproduce ENSO’s observed statistics, whether it captures variable dependence, and whether it forecasts the held-out years better than persistence. This dependence is tested by reconstructing withheld variables from observed ones.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Each test uses the period"
source_evidence.quote: Each test uses the period suited to it: a long record (1950–2019) for statistics, the reliably observed years 1980–2014 for reconstruction, and years the agents never saw (2015– 2024) for prediction. The agents receive only the 1980–2014 data, whereas the reference was developed with observations covering all three periods and was not tuned to this composite score.

harness.primary_contribution: SciExam for ENSO has agents turn raw ocean-atmosphere observations into five monthly ENSO indices, write and freeze their own diagnostics, and build a low-order stochastic model that hidden graders score against a published reference on statistics, withheld-variable reconstruction and held-out forecasts.

review_audit.title_checked: SciExam for ENSO: Can AI Agents Build Climate Models?
review_audit.claim_summary: SciExam for ENSO has agents turn raw ocean-atmosphere observations into five monthly ENSO indices, write and freeze their own diagnostics, and build a low-order stochastic model that hidden graders score against a published reference on statistics, withheld-variable reconstruction and held-out forecasts.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: Twelve agent systems (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, or Claude Code via OpenRouter, each paired with an LLM) run in offline containers with a six-hour budget on 1980-2014 data; the composite weights statistics on 1950-2019 (0.3), reconstruction on 1980-2014 (0.3) and 1-12-month forecasts on unseen 2015-2024 versus persistence (0.4), compared with a published five-variable reference model (0.378), plus single-run information controls for the top system.
corrections: The agent scaffolds are existing systems; the contribution is the benchmark protocol and graders rather than a new agent, and composite differences of about 0.01 should not be read as a ranking.

The memorization and information-access controls are single runs of the top system and are suggestive; agent models beat the reference through reconstruction and forecasting, while the reference still reproduces the observed statistics best.

citation.title: Lapras: Latent Reasoning for Time Series Language Models
citation.authors: Chen, Yuliang and Wu, Yu Yvonne and Langer, Patrick and Pillai, Arvind and Regmi, Sudarshan and Maritsch, Martin and Liu, Juncheng and Jakob, Robert and Kaar, Thomas and Griffin, Tess Z. and Marsch, Lisa and Heinz, Michael V. and Jacobson, Nicholas C. and Campbell, Andrew

claim.summary: Lapras post-trains time series language models to reason through six continuous thoughts in the joint time series-language space by aligning the student's answer-position hidden states with those of a jointly trained CoT-SFT teacher, decoding text only for the final answer.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "To address this limitation, we"
source_evidence.quote: To address this limitation, we propose Lapras, which adapts teacher-student self-distillation to post-train TSLMs for latent reasoning, letting the model learn from reference CoT while performing intermediate reasoning through continuous thoughts (Section 3.2).

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "In latent mode the student"
source_evidence.quote: In latent mode the student never samples a token. Instead, after each forward pass, it extracts the last hidden state zk at the final position and projects it back into the input embedding space via a small learned MLP π. The projected vector is then appended to the input sequence as if it were a new token embedding, and the model runs another forward pass.

harness.primary_contribution: Lapras post-trains time series language models to reason through six continuous thoughts in the joint time series-language space by aligning the student's answer-position hidden states with those of a jointly trained CoT-SFT teacher, decoding text only for the final answer.

review_audit.title_checked: Lapras: Latent Reasoning for Time Series Language Models
review_audit.claim_summary: Lapras post-trains time series language models to reason through six continuous thoughts in the joint time series-language space by aligning the student's answer-position hidden states with those of a jointly trained CoT-SFT teacher, decoding text only for the final answer.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: Five multiple-choice sensor QA tasks (ECG diagnosis, aero-engine fault diagnosis, HAR, sleep staging, TSR counterfactual prediction) on four TSLM backbones (ChatTS-7B, OpenTSLM-1B, SLIP-1B, ITFormer-0.5B); accuracy, macro-F1 and generated tokens against No-CoT, explicit CoT-SFT, iCoT and COCONUT, with ablations and decoded-thought analyses.
corrections: The method adapts an existing self-distillation latent-reasoning framework (Shen et al., 2025) to TSLMs and still needs reference CoT traces for the teacher, built from templates or generated by Qwen3.5-27B.
On ITFormer-0.5B every reasoning method, Lapras included, trails No-CoT in average F1; the work has no agent runtime, tool use or multi-step interaction.

citation.title: World2TS: Real-World Event Context for Time-Series Forecasting
citation.authors: Liu, Zhiding and Yang, Jiqian and Cheng, Mingyue and Li, Zhi and Chen, Enhong

claim.summary: World2TS uses an agent-led, CLI-validated and human-gated workflow to discover, consolidate and ground real-world events to individual series, producing a 31-dataset forecasting corpus with 1,159 events and 56,846 event-series links.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "The CLI tool serves as"
source_evidence.quote: The CLI tool serves as the execution and validation layer. The CLI materializes the workflow artifacts under fixed schemas, executes agent-authored searches across approved sources, records evidence and provenance, and maintains explicit budgets, caches, and resumable state.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Before publication, they examine the"
source_evidence.quote: Before publication, they examine the quality report together with the resulting events and event– series associations, checking that dates and evidence agree, scopes are appropriate, and unsupported causal claims are avoided. Each approval is bound to the reviewed artifacts, so subsequent changes invalidate the corresponding decision and require renewed review.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "In detail, the workflow partitions"
source_evidence.quote: In detail, the workflow partitions the dataset’s temporal coverage into search windows and specifies initial event themes. For each window, the agent proposes queries grounded in the series semantics, and the CLI executes the initial searches across the configured sources. All initial searches complete before the agent reviews the window, allowing evidence from different themes to inform a joint assessment.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "If refinement is needed, the"
source_evidence.quote: If refinement is needed, the agent issues one additional query based on the latest feedback. This query may cross the initial themes, for example by pursuing an institution or location identified in a retrieved report. Each refinement records its relationship to attempted queries and the evidence gap it addresses.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "On the other hand, for"
source_evidence.quote: On the other hand, for series grounding, temporal coincidence alone is insufficient to associate an event with a series. For each canonical event, the agent specifies an association rule over approved semantic dimensions, such as location or entity identity. The CLI applies the rule to series metadata and checks overlap between the event interval and each series’ temporal coverage.

claim.summary: OntoAR-HAR has an LLM descend a confusion-guided activity ontology, choosing a child at each node from node-constrained population and personal retrieval plus executable feature reports, and adds accepted query windows to a per-user memory through an agreement gate.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "For each sensor view, the"
source_evidence.quote: For each sensor view, the static population store Dg contains source embeddings and labels. A logical mask restricts retrieval at node v to examples whose labels occur below v: Rg (xq , v) = topk{s(eq , ei ) : yi ∈ leaf(v)}, (1) where eq and ei are encoder embeddings and s is cosine similarity. The indexes are physically shared but logically filtered, avoiding a separate database for every node.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "At node v, the context"
source_evidence.quote: At node v, the context Cv contains the local instruction πv , similar examples retrieved and fused from Dg and Dp , and the feature report. The LLM returns a child and a short evidence record: ĉv = arg max PLLM (c | Cv ). (3) c∈child(v) The agent moves to ĉv until reaching a leaf ŷ. This coarseto-fine path directly represents cases such as activity → locomotion → walking direction, so a feature is evaluated only

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "The personalized store Dp has"
source_evidence.quote: The personalized store Dp has the same representation but is initialized empty for each inference user. It contains previously observed query windows paired with accepted predictions. Retrieval first obtains the active labels from Dg and then searches Dp under the same label and node constraints.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "After prediction, a prompt-based gate"
source_evidence.quote: After prediction, a prompt-based gate decides whether (xq , ŷ) enters Dp . The gate checks agreement between static population retrieval, personal retrieval when available, and the node feature ranges; ambiguous or contradictory cases are not inserted.

source_evidence.quote: At each ambiguous node, an LLM proposes a structured list of feature names, physical interpretations, and calculations from the child labels and sensor metadata. On examples misclassified by retrievalonly inference, we test execution and measure separation by mean standardized feature distance to retrieved activity references.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "Meaning of activity-pair feature knowledge."
source_evidence.quote: Meaning of activity-pair feature knowledge. This is a description of sensor differences between two activities that are easily confused. During construction, the method reads source-domain acceleration, angular velocity, and retrieved reference examples for a registered pair; trains candidate tabular models; computes permutation importance; and selects the number of feature families on the independent source validation set.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "At the activity-pair stage, the"

citation.title: Agentic4PDM: Host-Governed Evidence Admissibility for Industrial Fault Diagnosis
citation.authors: Nguyen, Nam V. and Van Truong, Hoang and D., Hieu D. and Nguyen, Duy Khuong and Pham, Quang and Kieu, Tung

claim.summary: Agentic4PDM has role-separated LLM agents compare a sensor window with one labelled reference per class, then a Judge requests property-indexed signal-analysis tools while a deterministic Host gates requests, assigns evidence roles by reference preflight and admits the final fault class.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "Together, these conditions ensure that"
source_evidence.quote: Together, these conditions ensure that the Judge uses only offered tools, covers all declared properties, and does not revisit properties measured in earlier rounds. This prevents selective investigation and repeated requests for more favorable results. The Host checks all three conditions before execution. If any condition fails, the Judge must select again.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "The roles specify how a"
source_evidence.quote: The roles specify how a packet may be used, not how confident it is. A corroborative packet passed the preflight, so its class counts as checked evidence and can support a proposed class. An advisory packet failed it, so its class is unchecked: it may shape the Judge’s hypothesis and its next request, and may add support to a proposal, but should not by itself overturn another result.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Next, the SAgent picks a"
source_evidence.quote: Next, the SAgent picks a smoothing family for each channel, and the Host marks the stable and deviant regions of each smoothed signal. The CSAgent then removes channels that carry no useful information and gives each remaining channel c a priority tier, tier(c) ∈ {high, medium, low}; the Host checks this choice and may restore a removed channel.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "the NAAgent compares the query"
source_evidence.quote: the NAAgent compares the query’s stable region with the stable region of each reference, whereas the ABAgent compares its deviant region with the corresponding deviant region of each reference. Each Analyst report identifies a set of plausible classes and assigns each candidate a confidence level from {high, medium, low}, together with supporting and contradicting observations.

harness.primary_contribution: Agentic4PDM has role-separated LLM agents compare a sensor window with one labelled reference per class, then a Judge requests property-indexed signal-analysis tools while a deterministic Host gates requests, assigns evidence roles by reference preflight and admits the final fault class.

contributions.TSK: Contract-checked gated adjudication; Query-adaptive comparative evidence construction

citation.title: GIFT-Eval-CTX: A Benchmark For Contextual Forecasting Model Evaluation
citation.authors: Liu, Xu and Yan, Hanshu and Aksu, Taha and Pham, Quang and Qiao, Zhongzheng and Liew, Jun Hao and Savarese, Silvio and Sahoo, Doyen and Li, Junnan

claim.summary: GIFT-Eval-CTX builds 10,000 hard GIFT-Eval test windows annotated with structured Macro and Micro future effects through validator-gated discovery agents and a blind-first critic, and measures how well forecasters convert that verified context into numerical trajectories.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "the pipeline first runs independent"
source_evidence.quote: the pipeline first runs independent Macro and Micro Discovery Agents, each combining LLM reasoning with deterministic code validation. The LLMs identify informative regions, determine effects’ mechanism and boundaries, and submit proposals. Deterministic validation then checks the proposed type and type-specific criteria. If a proposal fails validation, the tool returns the numerical evidence so that the Agent can revise its proposal.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "Free-form descriptions confound the information"
source_evidence.quote: Free-form descriptions confound the information conveyed by a context with its wording, domain vocabulary, and level of detail. We instead represent future context through structured effects, a domain-agnostic key-value schema designed to be portable across models. Structured effects decompose the future into a single Macro description and a set of Micro effects.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Blind-first Joint Critic Agent. After"
source_evidence.quote: Blind-first Joint Critic Agent. After both discovery branches finish, a Joint Critic Agent reviews their outputs. The Critic first inspects the raw history and future while all outputs of the discovery agents remain hidden. Only after forming an independent interpretation can it view the proposed Macro and Micro effects, their explanations, and the corresponding numerical evidence.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "GIFT-Eval-CTX supports a paired evaluation"
source_evidence.quote: GIFT-Eval-CTX supports a paired evaluation of the same forecasting model under two information conditions. In the history-only condition, the model receives only (x1:T , H). In the contextual condition, it additionally receives s. Comparing the two conditions allows us to assess how effectively a model uses the supplied future context.

harness.primary_contribution: GIFT-Eval-CTX builds 10,000 hard GIFT-Eval test windows annotated with structured Macro and Micro future effects through validator-gated discovery agents and a blind-first critic, and measures how well forecasters convert that verified context into numerical trajectories.

contributions.TSK: Paired history-only and structured-context forecasting evaluation

citation.authors: Liu, Haoxin and Fu, Deqing and Fu, Lucheng and Jin, Yiqiao and Qiang, Rushi and Kamarthi, Harshavardhan and Prakash, B. Aditya

claim.summary: TimeRSI has a coding agent revise preprocessing, feature, context-selection and post-processing code around a frozen TSFM using window-level forecast errors, then selects among retained pipelines per origin from their errors on similar completed windows.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "The loop starts from direct"
source_evidence.quote: The loop starts from direct TSFM inference as the reference pipeline. In each iteration, the agent uses the task description and earlier results to propose and implement a code revision. The system executes it on the adaptation windows and returns forecasting scores, window-level errors, and execution logs.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "The evaluator supplies the same"
source_evidence.quote: The evaluator supplies the same chronological windows to all candidates. Candidate code receives no target values beyond each window’s origin. The agent can access the labels of the adaptation windows through evaluation feedback; these labels are not passed to the pipeline as prediction inputs.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "T IME RSI therefore selects"
source_evidence.quote: T IME RSI therefore selects a pipeline for each target variable at each new forecast origin. The selector describes the current conditions using numerical features of the recent history and reference forecast, including level changes, recent trends, and forecast shape. It retrieves similar completed windows and compares how the retained pipelines performed on them.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.8; passage beginning "For each candidate and historical"
source_evidence.quote: For each candidate and historical window, the loss is its mean absolute scaled error (MASE) divided by the reference MASE, with a denominator floor of 10−8 . MASE divides mean absolute forecast error by the mean absolute seasonal difference in the history available at that origin.

harness.primary_contribution: TimeRSI has a coding agent revise preprocessing, feature, context-selection and post-processing code around a frozen TSFM using window-level forecast errors, then selects among retained pipelines per origin from their errors on similar completed windows.

contributions.TSK: Origin-aligned deployment-pipeline revision; Similarity-weighted historical pipeline selection

review_audit.title_checked: TimeRSI: Towards Self-Improved Agentic Deployment for Time-Series Foundation Models
review_audit.claim_summary: TimeRSI has a coding agent revise preprocessing, feature, context-selection and post-processing code around a frozen TSFM using window-level forecast errors, then selects among retained pipelines per origin from their errors on similar completed windows.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: All 98 TIME and 100 FEV-bench tasks (111,177 and 235,039 forecast instances); MASE and CRPS on TIME and MASE/SQL/WQL/WAPE skill on FEV-bench against 32 and 31 published submissions, with a non-iterative-search ablation and swaps of coding agent (Antigravity) and backbone (Chronos-2, LPTM).
corrections: Gains over direct inference with the same frozen TimesFM 3.0 are small on TIME (MASE -1.52%, CRPS -1.61%), and leaderboard rankings use published submission results rather than re-run baselines.
The TSFM is never trained; the contribution is agent-written deployment code plus selection, and the authors note that historical-window gains need not carry to future forecasts.

citation.title: NeuroAct: Advancing EEG Analysis and Decoding via Dual-Loop Autonomous Research
citation.authors: Xiong, Wei and Li, Jiangtong and Zhao, Han and Yang, Linxiao and Li, Jie and Jiang, Changjun

claim.summary: NeuroAct coordinates prompted Researcher, Developer and Reviewer agents that analyse EEG signals and models, implement and run decoding interventions, and distil conditional recommendations that later EEG studies reuse and revise.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "Specialized collaboration. NeuroAct separates persona"
source_evidence.quote: Specialized collaboration. NeuroAct separates persona contexts and permissions so that scientific assessment, implementation, and review remain distinct. The Coordinator decomposes the objective into parallel questions and assigns each to a separate research cycle. The Researcher investigates an assigned question using literature, dataset semantics, and EEG evidence, then develops a feasible proposal.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Feedback redirects research. The Coordinator"
source_evidence.quote: Feedback redirects research. The Coordinator compares observed results and resource consumption with expected effects before selecting the next investigation. Reviewer challenges to an implementation or explanation can trigger further investigation.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Distillation from contrasting outcomes. The"
source_evidence.quote: Distillation from contrasting outcomes. The outer loop distills experience about which experimental actions help under particular task and model conditions. The Coordinator compares an intervention's expected and observed effects with considered alternatives, producing a conditional recommendation,

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Revision through subsequent research. Target"
source_evidence.quote: Revision through subsequent research. Target outcomes can narrow a recommendation, revise its action, or suspend its use. Matched trials assess transfer through performance and research cost.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.16; passage beginning "NeuroAct's EEG analysis tools provide"
source_evidence.quote: NeuroAct's EEG analysis tools provide signal summaries and configurable measurements for specific research questions. Spectral analysis uses Welch estimates and configurable frequency bands. Spatial analysis summarizes covariance and channel relationships. Domain-shift analysis compares permitted partitions. Computed signal descriptors include band power, Hjorth measures, spectral entropy, peak frequency, and regional summaries;

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.8; passage beginning "Full NeuroAct improves Workload BA"
source_evidence.quote: Full NeuroAct improves Workload BA by 11.51 points over registered recipes, demonstrating the value of interventions beyond parameter selection. Full exceeds the basic-statistics condition by 21.14 BA points on ADFTD and the primary-metric-only condition by 6.60 points on BCIC-IV-2a.

harness.primary_contribution: NeuroAct coordinates prompted Researcher, Developer and Reviewer agents that analyse EEG signals and models, implement and run decoding interventions, and distil conditional recommendations that later EEG studies reuse and revise.

contributions.GH: Coordinator-directed specialist research cycles; Conditional experience distillation and revision
contributions.GTS: EEG spectral and spatial signal-analysis tools

review_audit.evaluation_summary: BrainBench EEG analysis (four domains, difficulty-weighted macro score) plus cross-task, single-task and model-combination studies on Workload, BCIC-IV-2a, ADFTD, HMC and HBN (balanced accuracy, AUROC, Pearson r, MAE) under a 50M-token or 5-GPU-hour budget, with three LLM backends, CodeAct/BrainPilot/BrainAgent baselines, mechanism ablations and experience-transfer studies.
corrections: Diagnosis membership rests on ADFTD dementia classification; the other targets are workload, motor-imagery and sleep-stage classification and HBN age regression, and the paper states that clinical use is not validated.

Settings B-D baselines are author-adapted implementations and Setting A CodeAct/BrainAgent scores are source-reported; REVE pretraining overlaps HBN, so cross-agent gaps are not a fully controlled comparison.

citation.title: Zephyrus-R1: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Weather Reporting
citation.authors: Yu, Fengfei and Fisher, Marshall and White, Isadora and Varambally, Sumanth and Jafari, Yasaman and Yadav, Shivam and Bartlett, Samuel M. and Roj, Shawn and Moore, Benjamin J. and Warner, Michael D. and Han, Luyu and Xia, Zhirui and Watson-Parris, Duncan and Berg-Kirkpatrick, Taylor and Ma, Yian and Yu, Rose

claim.summary: Zephyrus-R1 trains tool-using vision-language weather agents with a two-stage curriculum, RL on verifiable weather-analysis questions followed by RL on report generation scored by a meteorological rubric and bidirectional claim entailment against NWS discussions and gated on evidence read at the current state and a forecast lead.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Direct report training must jointly learn"
source_evidence.quote: Direct report training must jointly learn tool use, weather analysis, and report composition from one scalar reward. We therefore use a two-stage curriculum: Stage 1 trains tool use on verifiable weather-analysis questions; Stage 2 optimizes report generation with the reward from Section 3.2.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "Both RL stages use CISPO with"
source_evidence.quote: Both RL stages use CISPO with group-centered advantages, 16 prompts and four rollouts per step, temperature 0.6, zero KL regularization, and rank-64 LoRA on the language layers with the vision tower frozen (Hu et al., 2022).

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "we require a minimum amount of"
source_evidence.quote: we require a minimum amount of successful tool use before assigning a judge-based reward. We maintain a binary grounding flag g(τ ) for each trajectory τ , which is set to one only if the agent has read a valid field from the current atmospheric state, obtained valid fields at a forecast lead, and received the resulting evidence in its context. Reports submitted before these conditions are satisfied are rejected, and the interaction continues.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "After review, we freeze a six-criterion"
source_evidence.quote: After review, we freeze a six-criterion rubric covering reference fidelity, spatiotemporal specificity, hazard prioritization, meteorological reasoning, thermal and precipitation-type plausibility, and calibrated use of detail. We then use this fixed rubric to score generated reports.

harness.primary_contribution: Zephyrus-R1 trains tool-using vision-language weather agents with a two-stage curriculum, RL on verifiable weather-analysis questions followed by RL on report generation scored by a meteorological rubric and bidirectional claim entailment against NWS discussions and gated on evidence read at the current state and a forecast lead.

contributions.TSK: Grounding-gated rubric and claim-entailment report reward

review_audit.title_checked: Zephyrus-R1: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Weather Reporting
review_audit.claim_summary: Zephyrus-R1 trains tool-using vision-language weather agents with a two-stage curriculum, RL on verifiable weather-analysis questions followed by RL on report generation scored by a meteorological rubric and bidirectional claim entailment against NWS discussions and gated on evidence read at the current state and a forecast lead.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: ERA5/WeatherBench 2 fields paired with NWS CONUS forecast discussions, training on 2,608 events from 1995-2018 and testing on 197 temporally disjoint 2019-2020 events; rubric score and Discussion F1 under the GPT-OSS-120B training judge and two independent judges, comparing Base, Direct RL and Curriculum RL for Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.8-27B against GPT-5.6-Luna and eight open-weight models, plus a 100-claim three-meteorologist audit of judge labels.
corrections: The forecaster tool is an oracle returning future ERA5 reanalysis fields, so the agent describes known atmospheric evolution rather than forecasting; scores do not reflect report quality under real numerical-forecast error.

All report scores are LLM-judge scores against NWS references, with the largest gains under the training judge; in the expert audit, judge-expert agreement is modest (Cohen's kappa 0.10-0.43) though comparable to inter-expert agreement.

citation.title: ACE-Trader: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Generator-Critic Trading Systems
citation.authors: Zhou, Chang and Zhou, Jiarun and Yu, Xingtong and Cheng, Hong and Zhang, Hui and Zhang, Xinming

claim.summary: ACE-Trader runs a Commit-Challenge-Revise loop between an LLM Trader and Red-Team, picks each role's memory with selectors trained online on memory-on versus memory-off net-return differences, and settles critiques and revisions against realized outcomes to build linked role-specific memories.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "Each selector combines a frozen"
source_evidence.quote: Each selector combines a frozen semantic encoder with an ensemble of trainable feedforward networks to score candidate memories using the current decision context, including market conditions, together with memory content and recorded outcomes.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "Once the outcomes are observed"
source_evidence.quote: Once the outcomes are observed, the net-return difference provides a shared binary label, with near-tied outcomes excluded. Each selector is trained on the saved representations of its selected memories using recency-weighted binary cross-entropy. The trading LLMs and semantic encoder remain frozen.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "We also check the risk"
source_evidence.quote: We also check the risk warnings in ct against the conditions and evaluation times specified before execution. A warning is a hit if the observed outcomes satisfy its stated condition under the specified evaluation rule. It is a false alarm if its evaluation horizon has ended and sufficient observations show that the condition was not satisfied.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "The Red-Team issues a challenge"
source_evidence.quote: The Red-Team issues a challenge only when current evidence contradicts a specific assumption in the Trader’s proposal. Each challenge includes suggested portfolio adjustments and a risk warning specifying an observable condition and when it should be evaluated.

harness.primary_contribution: ACE-Trader runs a Commit-Challenge-Revise loop between an LLM Trader and Red-Team, picks each role's memory with selectors trained online on memory-on versus memory-off net-return differences, and settles critiques and revisions against realized outcomes to build linked role-specific memories.

contributions.TSK: Net-return-trained context-dependent memory selectors; Outcome-settled Trader and Red-Team memory co-evolution

review_audit.title_checked: ACE-Trader: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Generator–Critic Trading Systems
review_audit.claim_summary: ACE-Trader runs a Commit-Challenge-Revise loop between an LLM Trader and Red-Team, picks each role's memory with selectors trained online on memory-on versus memory-off net-return differences, and settles critiques and revisions against realized outcomes to build linked role-specific memories.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: Daily trading of 33 U.S. equities with 2021-2023 FNSPID data for baseline training and warm-up and a 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30 test on FMP data with 5 bp costs; cumulative and annualized return, Sharpe, drawdown, volatility, hit rate and turnover against 22 active baselines in six categories (ML, RL, general and finance LLMs, single- and multi-agent trading systems) and two passive references, plus selector/co-evolution ablations and alpha/gamma sensitivity.
corrections: Cumulative return (+12.44%) is slightly below NASDAQ buy-and-hold (+12.82%); the advantage over the passive index lies in Sharpe, drawdown and volatility, not return.
Selector supervision requires running a second, memory-free copy of the full workflow at every step, and all reported results come from one six-month test window.

citation.title: Rethinking Agentic Model Orchestration for Time Series Forecasting
citation.authors: Guan, Tong and Zhan, Tianxiang and Pan, Shirui and Jin, Ming

claim.summary: FairAMO evaluates TSFM orchestrators on a frozen forecast bank where each must commit a selection or weights from a fixed backtest budget before test labels are revealed, separating orchestration ability from candidate-pool strength and complementarity.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "we introduce FairAMO, a controlled"
source_evidence.quote: we introduce FairAMO, a controlled evaluation protocol built on a Frozen Forecast Bank. Within each comparison, all orchestrators operate on the same candidate forecasts and receive the same explicitly specified historical evidence. Each orchestrator must commit to either a model selection or a set of combination weights before the test labels are revealed, and all resulting forecasts are evaluated using the official GIFT-Eval protocol.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "Before any test label is"
source_evidence.quote: Before any test label is revealed, the orchestrator receives the permitted evidence: the N most recent training backtests, plus the validation backtests if available. Using only this evidence, it produces an orchestration strategy, either a model selection or a set of combination weights, which is then committed and frozen for the test period. No rerun, reweighting, or inspection of test scores is permitted after commitment.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "• Headroom H(P ) ="
source_evidence.quote: • Headroom H(P ) = Lbest (P ) − Loracle (P ) is the accuracy that the differences between pool members put on the table. It is a property of the pool alone and does not depend on the orchestrator. • Gain G = Lbest (P ) − Lmethod (P ) is what a method actually recovers relative to the baseline. It is negative for a method that ends up worse than the best single TSFM, which several of the methods we evaluate do.

harness.primary_contribution: FairAMO evaluates TSFM orchestrators on a frozen forecast bank where each must commit a selection or weights from a fixed backtest budget before test labels are revealed, separating orchestration ability from candidate-pool strength and complementarity.

contributions.TSK: Frozen forecast bank with commit-before-reveal orchestration; Pool headroom and realization decomposition

citation.authors: Feng, Yebo and Dai, Jingyang and Pan, Liangrui and Lau, Nelson and Xu, Jiahua and Liu, Yang

claim.summary: Steward has analyst agents, a Portfolio Manager and a protected Risk Manager trade from typed reports and a code-assembled seven-layer memory, while evening code grading and a gated, replay-verified quarterly prompt-learning loop evolve the periphery around an invariant order-and-risk core.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "They share a memory that"
source_evidence.quote: They share a memory that code assembles from the system’s own record in seven layers, read by the Portfolio Manager every morning. L1 holds the day’s typed analyst signals. L2 gives each holding its entry date, days held, entry thesis and its last seven Technical ratings. L3 is the narrative: the last seven evening outlooks, seven days of macro regime, and the high-conviction news state changes of the last two weeks.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "The labels the Evening Analyst"
source_evidence.quote: The labels the Evening Analyst assigns are categories; every quantity that measures an outcome is computed by code from fills and prices. What feeds forward is aggregated by code from that record: the calibration of L4, the hit rates of the next-day calls, missed themes that recur in at least two episodes or symbols over the last 14 evenings, and root causes that recur across at least two symbols.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Edits are append-only into"
source_evidence.quote: Edits are append-only into the marked section and tagged with quarter and content hash, so human-written text is never modified; targets must be on the allow-list; a word-boundary tripwire rejects absolutes such as never, always and override, which conflict with the hard rules; a Jaccard similarity of 0.6 or more to an existing entry rejects a paraphrase;

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "A decision-replay harness passes"
source_evidence.quote: A decision-replay harness passes recorded inputs through the prompt before and after a learning, with the rest of the input fixed, and compares the outputs structurally: for the Portfolio Manager, which symbols were added, dropped or resized;

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "Hard rules run before the"
source_evidence.quote: Hard rules run before the LLM check. citation.authors: Charan, Geetha and Balasubramaniam, Vedant and Patil, Manojkumar and Priyanka, V. and Sathvik, Kodur Sai Vinay and Suresh, Rohit P and Azam, Mohammad Sufyan and Narahari, Y.

claim.summary: Agri-SCHOLAR issues weekly in-season irrigation and fertilizer advisories in which LLM agents set agronomically feasible action bounds and an optimizer searches within them, scoring each candidate with APSIM on a weather trajectory restricted to information available at the decision date.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "The key component of Agri-SCHOLAR"
source_evidence.quote: The key component of Agri-SCHOLAR is a novel LLM-bound optimization mechanism that assigns complementary roles to language agents and numerical optimization. LLMs define agronomically feasible action bounds, while the optimizer searches within those bounds using APSIM as an evaluation oracle.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "The VFA translates each candidate"
source_evidence.quote: The VFA translates each candidate action into APSIM tool calls and runs the simulation on the constructed weather file for the current cycle. It returns the resulting metrics (grain yield, soil water status, nitrogen balance, drainage, and leaching) to the OA, which computes the reward. It also returns them to the ABA, so that bounds can be tightened or relaxed if they repeatedly yield infeasible or dominated candidates.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "To emulate the information available"
source_evidence.quote: To emulate the information available to an operational advisory system, we construct the weather as follows: weather up to current date, a noisy seven-day forecast, and an analog-based estimate for the remainder of the season.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "The weather beyond the 7-day"
source_evidence.quote: The weather beyond the 7-day forecast is filled in with observed weather from a historical year that resembles the current season. The analog is selected using only information available up to the decision date.

review_audit.claim_summary: Agri-SCHOLAR issues weekly in-season irrigation and fertilizer advisories in which LLM agents set agronomically feasible action bounds and an optimizer searches within them, scoring each candidate with APSIM on a weather trajectory restricted to information available at the decision date.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: Eleven kharif maize seasons (2015-2025) in one irrigated and one rainfed South Asian region with ERA5 daily weather; weekly advisories are replayed in APSIM under realized weather and compared with the regional package of practices on yield, net profit, production cost and sustainability penalty, with loose-bound and no-bound ablations of the bounding agent (Gemma-4-E4B-it agents).
corrections: All outcomes are APSIM simulations (the simulator is not calibrated against field trials) and the seven-day forecast is a synthetic perturbation of observed weather, so the gains do not establish field yields or performance with operational forecasts.

In the irrigated-region ablation, loose expert-range bounds give higher mean yield and profit than the LLM bounds; the demonstrated benefit of the LLM bounding agent is a lower sustainability penalty and agronomically practical doses, not higher profit.

claim.summary: Vendster has two LLM agents negotiate per-product promotional discounts while the Buyer privately sees M5-grounded demand forecasts from ten model forecasters or a controlled bias and interval-width grid, measuring how forecast properties change sales-target attainment.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "We propose Vendster, an arena"
source_evidence.quote: We propose Vendster, an arena in which two LLM agents negotiate promotional discounts while the Buyer privately consumes a demand forecast, so a forecaster’s bias and prediction-interval width can be varied with the data-generating process, action space, and negotiation held fixed

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "The second is a synthetic"
source_evidence.quote: The second is a synthetic perturbation grid that scales true expected demand by a prescribed log-bias and interval-width factor, giving independent, causal control over the two error axes. Together they define 26 conditions: a no-forecast control, the 10 model forecasters, and a 15-cell grid

harness.primary_contribution: Vendster has two LLM agents negotiate per-product promotional discounts while the Buyer privately sees M5-grounded demand forecasts from ten model forecasters or a controlled bias and interval-width grid, measuring how forecast properties change sales-target attainment.

review_audit.title_checked: Vendster: An Evaluation Arena to Investigate How Forecasting Tool Quality Affects LLM Agent Behaviors in Buyer–Vendor Negotiation
review_audit.claim_summary: Vendster has two LLM agents negotiate per-product promotional discounts while the Buyer privately sees M5-grounded demand forecasts from ten model forecasters or a controlled bias and interval-width grid, measuring how forecast properties change sales-target attainment.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: Vendster-M5 with 16 five-product baskets and 25 episodes per condition across 26 forecast conditions; Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.6 Sol, DeepSeek-V3.2 and Qwen3-235B-A22B in self-play; sales-target attainment is tested with paired and per-basket slope t-tests under Holm correction against bias, interval width and relWQL/MASE/MAPE/sMAPE/RMSE/CRPS, with logged negotiation behaviours.
corrections: The agents do not forecast: they receive a month-4 point forecast with an 80% interval, a three-event history and a predicted-versus-actual track record in context, so the work evaluates forecast consumption rather than agent time series reasoning.
Conclusions rest on one elasticity, M5 demand and a single-event negotiation, and the null result for accuracy metrics holds only within the narrow near-ideal accuracy band of the model forecasters.

citation.title: The Athlete as a Scientist of One: Agentic Bayesian Experimental Design for Individualized Physiology from Consumer Wearables
citation.authors: Moradi, Behnam

claim.summary: EpiCoach runs a weekly agent cycle in which LLM agents propose hypotheses, template-constrained model refinements and workouts while deterministic tools fit a wrist-only digital twin, move beliefs only through logged fits and sealed predictions, and enforce training-load safety constraints.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.1; passage beginning "Claims about the athlete live"
source_evidence.quote: Claims about the athlete live in an evidence-gated hypothesis registry: each must issue a probabilistic prediction about a future session before it occurs, and its belief moves only through computed evidence from a logged statistical fit.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "Before every instrument ride the"
source_evidence.quote: Before every instrument ride the ledger holds a sealed prediction for it; a ride is scored by the first traversal after sealing, one traversal scores at most one prediction, and a ride through the gates without the lap protocol is training data and never scores. The twin is refit once per week, after all of that week's predictions have been scored and before the next are sealed

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.1; passage beginning "The agent prescribes the next"
source_evidence.quote: The agent prescribes the next training week as a constrained experiment maximizing information gain subject to load and safety constraints, around two instrument rides.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "What the agent designs is"
source_evidence.quote: What the agent designs is the training between them: one of fifteen one-, two- or three-week load patterns (conventional, front/back-loaded, deload 50/25/0%, overload 115/130% and their sequences), chosen by Eq. (2) and checked by the safety officer.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.1; passage beginning "Predictions come from a mechanistic"
source_evidence.quote: Predictions come from a mechanistic digital twin inferred from heart rate, GPS and barometric altitude: a lagged heart-rate response model, a fitness– fatigue model with learned time constants, and a latent technicaldescending skill state, measured on discovered trail segments.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.8; passage beginning "TABLE I: Rolling-origin replay, 60"
source_evidence.quote: TABLE I: Rolling-origin replay, 60 weekly origins, one-week horizon. CRPS (lower is better) with 95% moving-block bootstrap intervals; 90%-interval coverage; Diebold–Mariano p against the twin row of the same target (HAC variance, lag 4).

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.8; passage beginning "b) Agentic replay.: With the"
source_evidence.quote: b) Agentic replay.: With the fixed registry (invariants I7– I8), the hypothesis loop runs causally at every origin: base twin refit, Hypothesizer + Modeler/Critic against a frozen-clock registry, Statistician evaluates open hypotheses (directional claims by Savage–Dickey on the stored fit; structural specs by compiling a linear term and refitting)

Evidence is a single subject (an author) with a three-week live phase; the randomized information-directed versus conventional comparison has not started, so the benefit of information-directed design is not established.
