citation.title: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI
citation.authors: Yu, Minghan and Dai, Mengyu and Wen, Yixin and Yang, Haizhao

claim.summary: WxCrop is an LLM assistant that routes plain-language questions to tools computing causally selected daily county hazard indices from weather records and forecasts and a payout-calibrated crop-loss model, assembling every reported number from tool receipts.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.27; passage beginning "From a question it writes a"
source_evidence.quote: From a question it writes a structured request: which quantity, for which county, crop, date and hazard, and which tool answers it, the hazard index, the loss model, the crop map or the weather layers. The platform runs the tools and records each result as a receipt that holds the value, its unit, the data version and the filters applied.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.27; passage beginning "The reply is then assembled by"
source_evidence.quote: The reply is then assembled by the platform from these receipts, and the model words the sentences around them, so every number in an answer traces to one tool call and its sources. A hazard assessment returns two receipts, the index with its tier and the loss by crop group, and a tier is accepted only when it follows from the index value and the tier boundaries.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "Wind and rainfall mattered, and so"
source_evidence.quote: Wind and rainfall mattered, and so did their interaction, while the other candidates repeated these two, showed no signal or lacked data (Methods). H therefore multiplies a wind load, which grows with the square of the sustained wind as dynamic pressure does, by an amplifier that grows with rainfall (equation 1).

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.15; passage beginning "The study covers the 67 counties"
source_evidence.quote: The study covers the 67 counties of Florida for 2004–2024, the period for which the insured-loss records, the hurricane archive and the gridded weather archives overlap. The hazard index is computed for each county and day, and the loss model is fitted on county × crop-group × month units,

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.9; passage beginning "If the index is higher, the"
source_evidence.quote: If the index is higher, the assistant treats the day as a disaster of that kind and takes everything from the first step as inputs: which crops are present in the county, their growth stage on that day, and their vulnerability. These enter the loss model calibrated for that hazard, which returns the expected loss of each crop group as a percentage of its expected season value.

source_evidence.locator: PDF p.13; passage beginning "the damage fraction is recovered from"
source_evidence.quote: the damage fraction is recovered from the payout by the inversion described in Methods, which finds for each county, commodity and month the damage that would have produced the recorded payout under the deductibles held,

review_audit.title_checked: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI
review_audit.claim_summary: WxCrop is an LLM assistant that routes plain-language questions to tools computing causally selected daily county hazard indices from weather records and forecasts and a payout-calibrated crop-loss model, assembling every reported number from tool receipts.
review_audit.evaluation_summary: 67 Florida counties, 2004-2024, with USDA RMA cause-of-loss insurance records: hazard indices scored by AUC against recorded cyclone, freeze and severe-drought days or seasons (0.98, 0.99, 0.76); leave-one-year-out loss model reproduces summed storm-month losses within 2%, ranks county citrus production declines (rank correlation 0.63) and UF/IFAS county pairs (66% correct), with payout-probability Brier 0.177 versus 0.224 for historical frequency; the assistant is shown through Hurricane Ian, freeze and dry-heat case studies.
corrections: The LLM assistant (GPT-6 Sol) is not evaluated quantitatively; every reported check concerns the non-LLM hazard indices and loss model, and the assistant appears only in case-study screenshots.

Loss checks are strongest for hurricanes; freeze and dry-heat percentages are checked only against scarce records (extreme freezes a factor of two to five below reports), and outputs are county-level percentages on the insured-unit scale, not field-verified losses.
review_audit.notes: Identity and selected method/evaluation passages checked against local PDF text; not an independent reproduction of reported results.
